body.stem: Your organization enables self-service password reset. The exhibit shows the Notifications tab settings. One administrator has just reset their password using SSPR. You need to identify which accounts receive an email notification about this event.

exhibit.text:
SSPR Notifications tab
---------------------
Property                                          | Value
Notify users on password resets?                  | Yes
Notify all admins when other admins reset their passwords? | Yes

options.text: Users assigned the Authentication Policy Administrator role
Users assigned the Hybrid Identity Administrator role
Users assigned the Global Administrator role
Users assigned the Privileged Role Administrator role

explanation.correct: With the admin-notification option enabled, only accounts assigned the Global Administrator role receive an email to their primary email address when another administrator resets their password using SSPR.

perChoice.a: The Authentication Policy Administrator role manages authentication policy but does not receive the admin password reset notification emails.
perChoice.b: The Hybrid Identity Administrator role manages hybrid identity configuration but does not receive admin password reset notification emails.
perChoice.d: The Privileged Role Administrator role manages role assignments but does not receive the admin password reset notification emails.

body.stem: Your organization enables self-service password reset. The exhibit shows the current Authentication methods settings. Users with only the Microsoft Authenticator app registered are blocked from completing a password reset, even when 'Number of methods required to reset' is set to 1. You want to retain a one-method requirement and keep Microsoft Authenticator enabled. What is the minimum number of additional authentication methods that must be enabled?

exhibit.text:
SSPR Authentication methods page
--------------------------------
Property                          | Value
Number of methods required to reset | 1
Mobile app notification           | Enabled
Mobile app code                   | Enabled
Email                             | Not selected
Mobile phone                      | Not selected
Office phone                      | Not selected

options.text: Zero additional methods
One additional method
Two additional methods
Three additional methods

explanation.correct: When the SSPR policy includes Microsoft Authenticator and the number of methods required is set to 1, at least one additional authentication method must be selected. Authenticator cannot be the only method available when the requirement is one method.

perChoice.a: Zero additional methods is not allowed; Authenticator cannot be the only authentication method when the number of methods required is set to 1.
perChoice.c: Two additional methods satisfies the rule, but it is greater than the minimum; only one additional method is required.
perChoice.d: Three additional methods satisfies the rule, but it is greater than the minimum; only one additional method is required.

body.stem: Your organization has Microsoft Entra ID with a custom domain (contoso.com) and uses Microsoft Entra Connect to synchronize identities from on-premises Active Directory. An administrator holds the Authentication Policy Administrator role and uses SSPR to reset their password. The process requires more pieces of authentication data than for regular users, and rejects security questions. You need to identify why this behavior occurs.

exhibit.text:
Tenant configuration
--------------------
Property                              | Value
Custom domain configured              | Yes (contoso.com)
Microsoft Entra Connect in use        | Yes
Trial subscription elapsed            | More than 30 days
Assigned role                         | Authentication Policy Administrator

options.text: The one-gate reset policy applies because the account has an administrator role
The strong default two-gate reset policy applies because the account has an administrator role, and this policy can't be changed
The trial one-gate reset policy applies because the tenant is using a default domain
The custom password policy applies because contoso.com is configured

explanation.correct: When a Microsoft Entra administrator role is assigned to a user, a strong default two-gate password reset policy is enforced. The policy requires two pieces of authentication data and prohibits security questions, and this policy can't be changed.

perChoice.a: A one-gate reset policy does not apply to accounts with an administrator role under these conditions; the strong default two-gate policy applies instead.
perChoice.c: The trial one-gate policy does not apply because the tenant is using a custom domain and Microsoft Entra Connect is synchronizing identities.
perChoice.d: Configuring a custom domain does not introduce a special password policy that restricts administrator password resets in this way.

body.stem: Your organization is configuring SSPR for users. Users are required to register their authentication methods when signing in. The administrator wants to set the maximum supported interval for users to be asked to re-confirm their authentication information. The exhibit shows the current Registration page settings. What value should be set for 'Number of days before users are asked to re-confirm their authentication information'?

exhibit.text:
SSPR Registration page
----------------------
Property                                                            | Value
Require users to register when signing in                            | Yes
Number of days before users are asked to re-confirm their authentication information | 90

explanation.correct: The valid values for prompting users to confirm their authentication information range from 0 to 730 days. The maximum supported interval is 730 days.

perChoice.a: 30 days is within the supported range but is not the maximum supported interval.
perChoice.b: 90 days is the current value displayed in the exhibit; it is within the supported range but is not the maximum.
perChoice.c: 365 days is within the supported range but is not the maximum supported interval.

body.stem: Your organization synchronizes user accounts from an on-premises Active Directory to Microsoft Entra ID using pass-through authentication. The pass-through authentication agent is operational and SSPR is enabled for a group that includes these synchronized users. When these users try to recover their sign-in through SSPR, they receive a message asking them to contact their administrator. You need to enable a feature so these users can use SSPR to recover. Which feature must you enable?

exhibit.text:
Microsoft Entra Connect configuration
-----------------------------------
Property                              | Value
Authentication method                 | Pass-through authentication
Identity source                       | On-premises Active Directory
SSPR-enabled group                    | Hybrid-Users

options.text: Combined security information registration
Password writeback
Microsoft Entra ID Protection
Self-service sign-up for guests

explanation.correct: When a user's password is managed on-premises and SSPR writeback is not deployed, the user is asked to contact their administrator to reset their password. Enabling password writeback allows the user to proceed with the self-service workflow.

perChoice.a: Combined security information registration lets users register authentication methods at a single location; it does not propagate password changes to an on-premises directory.
perChoice.c: Microsoft Entra ID Protection provides risk-based conditional access and risk detections; it does not propagate password changes to an on-premises directory.
perChoice.d: Self-service sign-up for guests lets external users create accounts in a tenant; it does not propagate password changes to an on-premises directory.

body.stem: You have a Microsoft Entra tenant. An administrator runs the PowerShell command shown in the exhibit to disable SSPR for administrator accounts. You need to inform the administrator of the maximum amount of time this configuration change can take before the change applies across the tenant. Which value should you tell the administrator?

options.text: Up to 30 minutes
Up to 60 minutes
Up to 2 hours
Up to 24 hours

explanation.correct: The documentation states that policy changes to enable or disable SSPR for administrator accounts can take up to 60 minutes to take effect across the tenant.

perChoice.a: 30 minutes is shorter than the documented maximum latency for the admin SSPR policy change to apply.
perChoice.c: Two hours is longer than the documented maximum delay of 60 minutes for this SSPR administrator policy change.
perChoice.d: 24 hours is far longer than the documented latency; the change takes effect well within 24 hours.

body.stem: You have a Microsoft Entra tenant. The administrator is updating the SSPR policy to require additional authentication factors. The exhibit shows the current method count distribution for users in the SSPR-enabled group. After the policy change, which group of users will no longer be able to complete a password reset using SSPR?

options.text: Users with multiple authentication methods enrolled
Users with only one authentication method enrolled
Users with no authentication methods enrolled
No users in the group will be blocked

explanation.correct: The documentation defines what happens when the required number of methods is raised from one to two. When two methods are required, a user who registered only one method cannot reset or unlock. In the exhibit, the only tier affected is the group of users with exactly one method enrolled. Users with two or more methods enrolled can still complete a password reset.

perChoice.a: Users with multiple methods enrolled have at least two methods registered, so they can satisfy a two-method requirement and are not blocked.
perChoice.c: There is no tier with zero methods registered in this distribution, and the documentation concerns users who have registered fewer than the required number of methods.
perChoice.d: The group of users with exactly one method enrolled is below the new two-method requirement, so some users in the group will be blocked.

body.stem: You have a Microsoft Entra tenant with self-service password reset enabled for a security group. Users in the group have the Microsoft Authenticator app installed on their phones, using it to verify their identity during password resets. The exhibit shows the current SSPR Authentication methods policy. The administrator plans to update the policy so that two authentication methods are required, instead of one, for users to reset their password. Which capabilities will be available to users through the Microsoft Authenticator app after this change?

options.text: Only push notifications are available
Only verification codes are available
Both verification codes and push notifications are available
Neither push notifications nor verification codes are available

explanation.correct: The documentation describes the mobile app behavior under the SSPR policy. When administrators require two methods to reset a password, the Microsoft Authenticator app supports both verification codes and push notifications as available options for the mobile app factor. In contrast, with only one method required, verification code is the only option available.

perChoice.a: Push notifications alone are not the only option available; verification codes are also available once the policy requires two methods.
perChoice.b: Verification codes alone are not the only option available; push notifications are also available once the policy requires two methods.
perChoice.d: The documentation explicitly enables notification and code through the mobile app when two methods are required, so neither capability is blocked.

body.stem: You are enabling self-service password reset for the first time in a new Microsoft Entra tenant. You need to identify which settings tab in the Password reset blade contains each configuration option. Match each configuration option to the correct settings tab.

items.text: Enable or disable the SSPR scope across the tenant
Limit the verification factors users can choose and how many are required
Require users to provide contact info when they next sign in
Email users after their own password has been changed
Direct users to a helpdesk URL or email during the reset

explanation.correct: The Password reset blade is organized into five tabs (Properties, Authentication methods, Registration, Notifications, and Customization) and each one hosts a specific set of configuration options.

perChoice.a: Belongs in the Properties slot. The Properties tab contains the Self service password reset enabled setting, which lets you select None, Selected, or All.
perChoice.b: Belongs in the Authentication methods slot. The Authentication methods tab exposes Number of methods required to reset and the list of Methods available to users.
perChoice.c: Belongs in the Registration slot. The Registration tab contains the Require users to register when signing in setting, which prompts users during sign-in.
perChoice.d: Belongs in the Notifications slot. The Notifications tab contains the Notify users on password resets setting, which sends an email after a user changes their password.
perChoice.e: Belongs in the Customization slot. The Customization tab holds the Custom helpdesk email or URL setting used to direct users to a help link.

body.stem: You support a Microsoft Entra tenant that collaborates with external partners using B2B. You need to determine whether each external profile can use Microsoft Entra self-service password reset in your tenant. Match each profile to the resulting capability.

items.text: B2B guest whose home organization has its own Microsoft Entra tenant where the feature is enabled
Guest whose account comes from a personal consumer webmail provider such as Outlook.com

slots.label: Allowed to perform a password reset through the service
Cannot perform a password reset through the service

explanation.correct: Reset and change are fully supported for B2B guests from partner tenants that have the feature enabled. Guests whose accounts come from personal consumer webmail providers are explicitly unsupported.

perChoice.a: Belongs in the allowed slot. A B2B guest whose home tenant has the feature enabled can reset using the password reset policy applied by their home tenant.
perChoice.b: Belongs in the cannot slot. Personal consumer webmail accounts granted as guests, such as those from Outlook.com or Hotmail.com, cannot use the self-service reset service in this tenant.

body.stem: The SSPR policy in your Microsoft Entra tenant requires two authentication methods to reset. A user is registered with multiple authentication methods. You need to determine how each combination of registered methods is counted toward the two-method requirement. Match each registered combination to the resulting count.

items.text: Microsoft Authenticator push notification combined with a software OATH token
Microsoft Authenticator push notification combined with an email one-time passcode
Software OATH token combined with a hardware OATH token
Email one-time passcode combined with a mobile phone number for SMS

slots.label: Counts as a single authentication method
Counts as two distinct authentication methods

explanation.correct: Microsoft Authenticator, software OATH tokens, and hardware OATH tokens all count as a single authentication method even when multiple are registered. Methods from different categories (such as a token and an email contact) count as separate methods.

perChoice.a: Belongs in the single count slot. Authenticator and a software OATH token are both in the same group of token-like methods and count as the same single authentication method.
perChoice.b: Belongs in the two distinct slot. Authenticator is one category and an email passcode is a different contact-based method, so the two methods count as separate factors.
perChoice.c: Belongs in the single count slot. Software and hardware OATH tokens are both in the same token-like group and count as the same single authentication method.
perChoice.d: Belongs in the two distinct slot. An email passcode and an SMS passcode are different contact methods and each counts as its own authentication method.

body.stem: You are configuring the Properties tab of the Password reset blade for a new Microsoft Entra tenant. The administrator needs to control which set of users in the tenant can use the self-service password reset feature. Match each value of the SSPR Enabled setting to the resulting scope of users.

items.text: Set SSPR Enabled to Selected and choose one Microsoft Entra group

slots.label: No users in the tenant are enabled for SSPR
Limits SSPR to a subset of users based on a chosen directory object
Every user in the tenant is enabled for SSPR

explanation.correct: The Properties tab offers three scope choices: None disables SSPR for everyone, Selected limits it to members of a chosen Microsoft Entra group (and nested group members), and All enables it for the entire tenant.

perChoice.a: Belongs in the None slot. Choosing None turns SSPR off for the entire tenant and no users can use the feature.
perChoice.b: Belongs in the Selected slot. Choosing Selected enables SSPR only for members of the chosen Microsoft Entra group, including members of any nested groups within it.
perChoice.c: Belongs in the All slot. Choosing All enables SSPR for every user account in the tenant.

body.stem: Your organization is rolling out Microsoft Entra self-service password reset (SSPR) to a pilot group. You need to give each pilot user the correct Microsoft portal URL based on what they need to accomplish. The pilot includes users who have not yet enrolled, users who are locked out of their account, users who need to install a phone-based verification application, and users who want to maintain their previously configured sign-in methods. Match each user need to the correct Microsoft portal URL.

slots.label: An end user has never enrolled authentication methods and wants to enroll before they sign in for the first time
An end user is locked out of their account and cannot access the applications they need
An end user wants to install a mobile verification application on their phone for the first time
An end user has previously set up their sign-in configuration and wants to maintain their list of active methods

explanation.correct: Microsoft Entra exposes dedicated portal URLs for each step of the SSPR and authentication experience. The standalone SSPR registration portal (https://aka.ms/ssprsetup) is used for first-time enrollment before sign-in. The main SSPR portal (https://aka.ms/sspr) is where users begin the unlock or password reset workflow. The mobile app setup portal (https://aka.ms/mfasetup) is for installing the Microsoft Authenticator app on a device. The combined security info registration page (https://aka.ms/setupsecurityinfo) is the unified interface for managing all authentication methods over time.

perChoice.url-ssprsetup: Belongs in the first-time enrollment slot: this is the standalone SSPR-only registration portal where users enroll their authentication methods before they sign in.
perChoice.url-sspr: Belongs in the locked-out slot: this is the main SSPR portal where users enter their account information and a CAPTCHA to begin the unlock or password reset workflow.
perChoice.url-mfasetup: Belongs in the install-app slot: this is the portal where users register their mobile application (such as Microsoft Authenticator) for use with SSPR and multi-factor authentication.
perChoice.url-setupsecurityinfo: Belongs in the modify-existing slot: this is the combined security info registration page where users view, change, add, or remove authentication methods after initial enrollment.

body.stem: Your tenant still shows a list of verification options on the Password reset blade, but since 30 September 2025 you can no longer add, remove, or change that list in that place. You want those options to remain enforced for the tenant going forward. Which action should you take?

options.text: migrate the settings to the Authentication methods policy
migrate the settings to the legacy multifactor authentication policy
migrate the settings to the tenant authorization policy
migrate the settings to the password reset properties page

explanation.correct: The tutorial states that managing authentication methods in the legacy multifactor authentication and self-service password reset policies is deprecated, and that beginning 30 September 2025 they can no longer be managed there. Customers are told to use the manual migration control to move to the Authentication methods policy by the deprecation date, so the configuration on the legacy blade must be migrated there.

perChoice.action:b: The legacy multifactor authentication policy is deprecated at the same time as the legacy self-service password reset policy, so it is not a valid destination for the settings.
perChoice.action:c: The tenant authorization policy stores the AllowedToUseSspr property that governs whether administrator accounts can use self-service password reset; it does not store the user verification options.
perChoice.action:d: The password reset properties page is the same legacy surface where these options can no longer be added or changed.

body.stem: A member of staff can no longer sign in after too many failed attempts and recovers the account through the self-service portal. When asked for a new password, the user types the same one they used immediately before the lockout, and the portal accepts it. You need to confirm that this matches expected behavior for the tenant. Which statement is correct?
body.statement: The portal accepted the value because {{reason}}.

options.text: a voluntary change blocks reuse of the previous password but a recovery does not
a recovery blocks reuse of the previous password but a voluntary change does not
both a voluntary change and a recovery block reuse of the previous password
neither a voluntary change nor a recovery blocks reuse of the previous password

explanation.correct: The password policy settings list password change history and password reset history as separate properties. Password change history stops a user from reusing the previous password when they change a password, while password reset history allows the last password to be used again when a user resets a forgotten password. So accepting the previous password during a portal recovery is expected.

perChoice.reason:b: This reverses the rule: reuse is blocked for a voluntary password change, not for a recovery of a forgotten password.
perChoice.reason:c: Recovering a forgotten password can reuse the previous password, so it isn't blocked in both cases.
perChoice.reason:d: A voluntary password change does stop the previous password from being used again, so at least one of the two cases is blocked.

body.stem: You disabled self-service password reset for administrator accounts in the tenant. The exhibit shows the resulting configuration. People who hold an administrator role still get an interruption during every interactive sign-in telling them they can't store any verification details. You need that interruption to stop appearing for them. Which change should you make?

rows: Password reset - Self service password reset enabled
Group chosen for the Selected scope
4 accounts holding Microsoft Entra administrator roles and 40 accounts holding none
Registration - Require users to register when signing in

body.statement: To stop the prompt, the administrator should {{change}}.

options.text: remove the administrator accounts from the group SSPR is enabled for
remove the non-administrator accounts from the group SSPR is enabled for
add the administrator accounts to the group SSPR is enabled for
remove the administrator accounts from the included group in the Authentication methods policy

explanation.correct: When the password reset policy for administrators is disabled through the tenant authorization policy (AllowedToUseSspr set to false), administrators can't reset their passwords through SSPR even if they fall inside the user password reset scope. If registration is required and they are in that scope, they are still interrupted at sign-in but see a message saying they can't register any methods. The documented remedy is to explicitly exclude administrators from the password reset policy for users, which in the admin center means the group the feature is enabled for.

perChoice.change:b: The accounts without administrator roles are the ones who can still use the feature, so removing them would remove working functionality instead of stopping the administrator prompt.
perChoice.change:c: The administrator accounts are already in the scope group, so adding them changes nothing and the interruption continues.
perChoice.change:d: The included group in the Authentication methods policy controls where the centralized policy applies; it doesn't determine the scope that drives this prompt on the Password reset blade.

body.stem: You must roll out self-service password reset to two separate pilot groups, HR-Pilot and Finance-Pilot, and keep the rollout limited to those pilots. The group picker on the Password reset blade in the Microsoft Entra admin center takes a single group at a time. Which approach should you use?

options.text: make one of the groups a member of the other
assign both groups to the same administrative unit
apply a dynamic membership rule to both groups
convert both groups into a single directory role

explanation.correct: The tutorial notes that the admin center can enable one Microsoft Entra group for self-service password reset, and that as part of a wider deployment the service supports nested groups. Putting one pilot group inside the other lets a single selection in the group picker cover both sets of users while keeping the rollout limited to them.

perChoice.approach:b: Administrative units organize directory objects for management purposes; they don't determine which users the self-service password reset setting applies to.
perChoice.approach:c: Dynamic membership rules populate a group from directory attributes such as department, but each rule fills its own group and doesn't let a single selection cover two separate groups.
perChoice.approach:d: Directory roles assign privileges to administrators; they have no effect on which users are in scope for self-service password reset.

body.stem: Some accounts in your tenant authenticate against an external directory, and their passwords are synchronized to the cloud copy. After one of these users recovers an account through the self-service portal, the page reports success, but the new value is rejected at sign-in for roughly two minutes. You need to explain the delay. Which statement explains it?

options.text: the change only updates the external directory and copying back into Microsoft Entra ID runs on a fixed interval
the portal waits for the user's phone to confirm the second factor before the change is applied
the change is queued until an administrator approves it in the admin center
the delay ends once the user's group membership is copied from the external directory

explanation.correct: For federated accounts whose passwords are synchronized, the source of authority stays in the external directory, so the portal updates the password only there. Synchronization back to Microsoft Entra ID is scheduled every two minutes, which is why the new value isn't accepted right away.

perChoice.reason:b: The second factor proves identity before the change; it isn't a step that runs afterwards, so it causes no delay.
perChoice.reason:c: Self-service password reset finishes without an administrator approval step, so nothing waits in a queue.
perChoice.reason:d: Membership data doesn't carry the new password to the cloud; the wait comes from the fixed interval for copying password changes.

body.stem: Your company uses Microsoft Entra ID with an on-premises Active Directory synchronized through Microsoft Entra Connect. Password writeback is enabled and SSPR is turned on for the HR-Pilot group. Locked-out employees report that the SSPR portal forces them to pick a new password each time they try to recover access. You need a configuration change so employees can recover access while keeping the existing password.
body.statement: To achieve this, set the {{setting}} option to {{value}} on the Password reset blade.

options.text: Allow users to unlock accounts without resetting their password
Notify users on password resets
Write back passwords to on-premises
Number of authentication methods required
Yes
No

explanation.correct: The 'Allow users to unlock accounts without resetting their password' option, when set to Yes, gives users a separate choice to unlock their on-premises account without going through a password reset. The No value combines unlock with a forced password reset, which is the symptom the locked-out employees describe.

perChoice.setting:b: Notify users on password resets controls email notifications sent to the user's primary and alternate addresses when a reset happens; it does not affect whether an unlock can happen independently of a reset.
perChoice.setting:c: Write back passwords to on-premises enables cloud-to-on-premises password synchronization and is already enabled in the scenario; it does not separate unlock from reset.
perChoice.setting:d: Number of authentication methods required sets how many challenge methods the user must complete during a reset or unlock; it does not control whether an unlock can occur without a reset.
perChoice.value:b: No disables the option, leaving the default behavior where a reset always unlocks the account on the same step, instead of offering an unlock-only path.
